findings.title: MOCI's Q2 2026 report posts 93–96% citizen satisfaction across digital and in-person channels
findings.summary: Qatar's Ministry of Commerce and Industry reported strong Q2 2026 performance across its digital-services and consumer-protection remit: 131,269 total transactions processed, 86% of them completed electronically, alongside a 93% satisfaction rate for online applications and 96% for applications handled at physical Government Services Centres. The ministry deployed 15 new digital services during the quarter, issued 6,745 new commercial registrations and registered 5,272 foreign companies. On consumer protection, of 9,511 complaints received, 7,808 concerned consumer-protection matters, with most resolved within five working days and 83,339 inspection visits completed to monitor market compliance. The gap between online (93%) and in-person (96%) satisfaction is a small but real signal for members benchmarking omnichannel government CX, the physical-channel edge suggests Qatar's Government Services Centres still out-perform the digital front door on experience quality, even as electronic completion rates climb.

findings.title: ServiceNow and Aramco Digital sign AI-powered enterprise-transformation agreement
findings.summary: Signed on LEAP 2026's closing day in Riyadh, the collaboration agreement between ServiceNow and Aramco Digital aims to standardise digital workflows across Aramco's distributed network spanning 50+ countries, building "a consistent AI-enabled foundation that can scale across the ecosystem." The agreement spans four domains: AI-powered workflows (intelligent automation to cut manual processes), customer experience (unified, CRM-driven service-management standards across entities), group shared services (reducing redundancy), and ERP modernisation (retiring legacy technical debt). ServiceNow's platform, which the company says now handles over 100 billion workflows annually, provides the governance and orchestration layer. The explicit naming of "customer experience" as one of four transformation pillars, not just an efficiency play, is the notable detail for MECSC members: it's a large-scale example of a Gulf enterprise treating CX standardisation as core infrastructure work rather than a bolt-on, at a moment when most GCC AI headlines skew toward government or retail rather than enterprise B2B service management.

findings.title: Primark opens its first Bahrain store at City Centre Bahrain on 23 September
findings.summary: Primark, via its partnership with Alshaya Group, confirmed today that its first Bahrain store will open at City Centre Bahrain on 23 September, stocking womenswear, kidswear, accessories, beauty and homeware under the retailer's "trend-led fashion, everyday essentials and unbeatable value" positioning. Opening day is planned around "entertainment, giveaways and activations designed to create a memorable shopping journey", a deliberate experience-led launch rather than a quiet stock-and-open. The announcement also confirmed that Primark's existing Mall of the Emirates store will add a second floor in November 2026 (expanding menswear and home ranges), and that further GCC entries into Kuwait and Qatar are planned for 2027. Useful for members tracking Alshaya's GCC retail-rollout playbook and how international value-fashion brands are using launch-day programming, rather than just store openings, as a customer-experience differentiator.

findings.title: Government-funded wholesale/retail trade complex under construction in Batken
findings.summary: A four-phase wholesale and retail trade complex is under construction in Batken, funded via a government programme allocating roughly 500 million som per year to regional infrastructure. The first block has been completed; three further phases are planned, including roads, utilities and additional parking for the new market complex. Developer/operator not named in the source reviewed.

findings.title: Official count: Kyrgyzstan operates 317 public markets and 94 shopping centres nationwide
findings.summary: A rare official retail-infrastructure census figure for a country still thin in this series' coverage: government data cited by AKIpress puts Kyrgyzstan's nationwide count at 317 public markets and 94 shopping centres. Full supporting detail was paywalled at the time of review, only the headline statistic could be independently confirmed.

findings.title: New Osh Bazaar: 155,000 sqm relocation project for Bishkek's central market
findings.summary: A planned "New Osh Bazaar", a 155,000 sqm, two-storey complex with more than 10,000 retail units, is intended to replace Bishkek's central Osh Market. President Sadyr Zhaparov inspected the site and cited a target completion of August 2026. Distinct from Bishkek Arena Mall (already carried in this series, 10 Jul 2026), a separate, stadium-linked retail development. Carried here as historic context (>90 days old) given the project's scale and presidential-level profile, and because it has not previously appeared in this report series.

findings.title: Lulu Group to invest BD62m in six new Bahrain stores, marking 20 years in the market
findings.summary: Lulu Group (member) announced a BD62 million (~US$164m) investment to open six new stores across Bahrain, marking two decades of operations in the country. Chairman Yusuff Ali M.A. said the six stores would be spread across different parts of Bahrain; the group currently operates 13 locations there. The announcement was made at an event at Dana Mall, Manama, attended by Deputy Prime Minister Shaikh Khalid bin Abdulla Al Khalifa.

findings.title: Standard Chartered Pakistan and Dolmen Group partner on home-financing benefits at Grove Residency
findings.summary: Standard Chartered Bank Pakistan and Dolmen Group (member) launched a partnership offering exclusive Saadiq Home Finance benefits to buyers of Dolmen's Grove Residency development near the KPT Interchange, Karachi; eligible clients can save at least PKR 5 million. Note: this is a residential-financing tie-up rather than a mall/retail-property announcement, included as a dated, in-window development directly involving the member company, distinct from Dolmen's shopping-mall operations (Dolmen Mall Clifton/Tariq Road).

findings.title: Cenomi Centers upsizes Riyad Bank facility to SAR2.7bn for Westfield Riyadh; opening guidance shifts to Q4 2026
findings.summary: Cenomi Centers (member) upsized a Shariah-compliant Murabaha financing facility from Riyad Bank to SAR2.7 billion to fund continued construction of Westfield Riyadh, the group's under-construction lifestyle and entertainment mega-project. Separately, per an Aug 9 CEO interview reviewed for background context only, the project's public opening guidance has shifted to Q4 2026, superseding an earlier "September" target cited in Feb 2026, not separately actioned as its own finding. Distinct from the previously-reported Al Madinah/Saudi Downtown Company deal and CMA capital-increase approval, both already carried in this series since mid-August.
